section_contracts.title: Informed Consent / Subject Enrollment

fixed_boilerplate.text: This retrospective study uses existing records.

content_expectations: Describe the approved record-review or enrollment sequence, time points, and timeline. State the supplied consent authorization, including an IRB-approved waiver when the approved source explicitly provides one. Preserve supplied retention, withdrawal, and replacement facts without implying that retrospective chart abstraction includes participant contact unless the source establishes it. Do not invent an IRB waiver or its timing.
Do not replace supplied detail with generic clinical prose.

This section owns supplied specimen handling and results-return policies. Preserve collection/coding, transfer recipients and access limits, testing purpose, specimen destruction timing and any absolute deadline, future-use/sharing/sale/commercial restrictions, and the distinction between specimen retention and derived-data retention. Distinguish individual clinical results, research/genetic results, incidental findings and aggregate summaries, including any limits, preferences, recipients and timing. Keep routine-care referral arrangements when supplied. Preserve uncertainty; absent optional policies remain absent. For records-only research, describe only the approved existing records/specimens and results policies without adding collection or participant contact.

This retrospective section owns the complete supplied record-abstraction methods and assessment details: instruments and scales, source restrictions, date anchors/windows, value selection and tie rules, ambiguous/missing values, event definitions, deduplication and evidence needed to establish zero or absence. Preserve every unique condition and exception here, with concise summaries elsewhere. Also explain supplied staff work phases, record and study completion triggers, and permission-suspension/resumption policies. These are staff tasks and historical windows, not participant visits. The retrospective template has no separate measurement section or assessment matrix; present these details as prose or lists within this section.

constraints: The Source-of-Truth is approved and source intake is closed. Do not request additional reviewer input.

Use only supplied approved evidence and applicable template/Fixed Clinical Boilerplate. Align shared population, groups, quantities, timing, procedures and outcomes across the Protocol, selected ICF and PRS narratives; preserve relationships and qualifications rather than copying wording.

Listed Fixed Clinical Boilerplate is authorized only where applicable and consistent with the approved source. The approved source supersedes boilerplate; boilerplate must not expand decision-making authority, termination grounds, completion criteria, procedures, or safety obligations.

When a section lists both Fixed Clinical Boilerplate and minimum evidence, include all material source facts and only applicable, nonconflicting boilerplate; omit boilerplate clauses that would alter a source rule.

Do not invent study-specific facts, procedures, risks, benefits, safety obligations, legal promises, or regulatory claims. Routine-use and record-review studies acquire no additional visits, monitoring or follow-up commitments from boilerplate.
Preserve supplied numbered citations next to the Protocol claims they support and their bibliography linkage. Do not invent citations; ICF explanations use plain language.
Return exactly one result for every requested section ID.
Use only the drafted or fixed_boilerplate outcome. Sparse sections may use only applicable, source-consistent listed Fixed Clinical Boilerplate.
Return structured section content, not a whole document or document markup.

Write to each section's purpose and ownership. Explain each operational rule fully in its owning section; elsewhere give only the fact needed for that section and a brief reference to the owning heading. Preserve necessary identifiers, endpoint definitions, quantities, timing anchors/windows, conditions, exceptions, safety information and client consent language. Compress repeated explanations, not clinical meaning.
Use participant-facing language for ICF sections.

writing_examples illustrate prose and organization using synthetic inputs. Draft from this request's approved_source and section_contracts; example facts are never study evidence or boilerplate. Return the requested response format.
For icf.key-information-summary, draft directly from its canonical summary obligations; keep each concept concise and never copy a complete detailed-section sentence or paragraph.

For a Sterling ICF, BACKGROUND owns lens descriptions, comparative evidence, the evidence gap, and rationale. PURPOSE must be concise and limited to the purpose, hypothesis, and primary endpoint; do not restate BACKGROUND.

ICF PROCEDURES owns detailed study activities and DURATION owns timing. Do not repeat their detail in PURPOSE, ALTERNATIVE TREATMENTS, VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION/WITHDRAWAL, or the participant statement unless the Sterling Clause Contract explicitly requires it.

For Protocol sections, follow concept_ownership: explain owned concepts completely, keep brief_reference_only concepts concise, and do not re-explain do_not_restate concepts. Endpoint names, visit names and timing, identifiers, quantities, safety terms, and brief traceability cross-references may recur.

Use protocol_writing_plan for the active Protocol headings and method/completion owners. General Information is a compact synopsis; Objectives states purpose; Study Design owns comparisons and endpoints; Bias explains why controls matter. Place full operational rules in the named active methods_owner and completion rules in completion_owner, even when their heading differs by branch. Statistical Methodology owns calculations/models. Cross-reference only a heading listed in the plan. When assessment_table_owner is null, describe the historical windows and activities in prose or lists rather than claiming a matrix or columns are rendered.

Satisfy every section's content_expectations and cover every material value named by minimum_evidence. If the writing plan names an assessment_table_owner, its source-derived table and notes carry that inventory and adjacent prose only introduces it. Otherwise the active methods_owner carries the full historical assessment details in prose or lists.

Write standalone clinical content that serves the section purpose. Refer to the study and its procedures directly, rather than to the synopsis, approved source, or drafting process. Preserve genuine numbered instruments/forms, citations and explained footnotes; remove a suspected orphan marker only when its source context supports that interpretation. Omit self-referential filler and redundant narration. These editorial preferences are not publication gates.

Use reference_detail_target_words only as a soft compression signal; independent AI review assesses substantive completeness, and concise complete prose must not be padded, repeated, or invented to meet a length target.
Explicitly distinguish the study objective, hypothesis, and endpoints when they describe different constructs.
When the approved source does not define an instrument, scoring rule, denominator, missing-data method, date, or version, do not invent one or expose an internal source-gap note.
Do not use an evidence reference unless the returned prose or list actually contains the material fact it supports.

Every paragraph object and every list object must include at least one evidence_refs or boilerplate_refs value allowed by its section contract. If prose only introduces an already-cited list, omit that paragraph instead of returning empty reference arrays.

source.filename: Form Fill Fillout -_ Generate Protocol + Send Gmail.json

adapter_instructions: For each mapped target, use its retained n8n messages as the base writing prompt. Produce only the named legacy field's content for that native section.

Return the current request's section_results or narrative schema, identifiers and evidence references. The old JSON aliases and section numbers are transport examples; the current template owns headings, numbering, tables and formatting.

A list group may contain a nonempty label alongside items. That label renders as an unbulleted paragraph immediately before the group's items; use it to separate endpoint categories without turning introductions into bullets.

This experiment checks response bindings, section inventory and text/list shape only. Evidence references may be retained for manual inspection; schedule_interpretation, benefit_interpretation and assessment_presentation bookkeeping is optional. The source-derived table is built directly from approved source rows.

Approved source facts and current section content_expectations (including Brad's corrections) override conflicting legacy instructions and demonstrations. Demonstration studies are examples, never evidence for this study.

Apply editorial_corrections only to their named target sections. They refine the retained n8n writing prompts; supplied study facts and applicable client consent language remain authoritative. Missing optional source detail is not a reason to expand or invent clinical content.

Use protocol_writing_plan and the current section ownership instructions to tighten the retained prompts: keep Protocol synopses brief, explain each operational rule fully in its owning section and use brief heading references elsewhere. Endpoint definitions and analysis calculations remain complete where needed; ICF explanations remain self-contained for participants. Preserve every material quantity, window, exception and safety qualification.
